paper.citation: Thorlund K, Imberger G, Walsh M, Chu R, Gluud C, Wetterslev J, Guyatt G, Devereaux PJ, Thabane L. The number of patients and events required to limit the risk of overestimation of intervention effects in meta-analysis—a simulation study. PLoS ONE 6(10):e25491 (2011).

inputs.name: PMC3196500 supplementary files (Europe PMC zip): Fig. 2 (pone.0025491.g002.jpg), Figs S1-S12 (pone.0025491.s001-s012.tif), Tables S3-S4 (s016.doc, s017.doc)

items.label: Fig. 1 (flowchart of the 36 scenarios)

cause.summary: A flowchart of the simulation design. Its settings (36 scenarios, 20,000 meta-analyses of 100 trials each) are the ones our simulation runs.

items.label: Fig. 2, upper panel (Cochrane trial sizes, PC 5-15%, tau2 0.15, true RRR 0%, cumulative patients)

assumptions.what: Zero cells: 0.5 added to every cell of a trial with a zero cell (or an arm with every patient an event); trials with no events in either arm (or only events) left out
assumptions.sensitivity: Keeping double-zero trials with the correction: Table 1 82 of 144 cells as printed against 81

assumptions.what: Events drawn as Binomial(arm size, P) with arm size n/2 rounded up (Appendix S2 writes bin(n_i, P))
assumptions.sensitivity: Binomial(n, P) on the whole trial: Table 1 10 of 144 cells as printed, 40 within one bin

assumptions.what: Trial sizes drawn as integers, uniform on each size interval (Table S2; 'common': 20-200 and 201-500); PE = PC x RR capped at 1; trials in draw order
assumptions.sensitivity: Not varied

assumptions.what: Seeds: numpy SeedSequence(3196500) per scenario; the paper gives none
assumptions.sensitivity: A second run with other seeds is compared cell by cell and panel by panel

assumptions.what: Binning of the curves: 'nearest' for patients (each estimate counts at the point its cumulative count rounds to), 'interval' for events
assumptions.sensitivity: Mean panel score, patients: nearest 0.6505, interval 0.5361; events: nearest 0.5878, interval 0.6721

assumptions.what: Point spacing: 500 patients (200 for PC 15-40% and 40-80%, where the published curves start at 200), 50 events
assumptions.sensitivity: The 'one point right' near-miss control in each panel

assumptions.what: Pixel map fitted to the tick marks and the printed tick labels (log x axis, 1-2-5 ticks; y ticks every 0.05)
assumptions.sensitivity: Fit residuals in figures.json (at most 1.4 px in Fig. 2, 0.6 px in the supplement)

cause.summary: Our curves score 55.4% within 2 px (pass mark 73.6%); our two runs score 77.8% against each other.
